officialInventory.summary: The Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA, Nature Conservation Sector) maintains the official list of natural protectorates declared by Prime Ministerial decree under Law No. 102 of 1983. Its July 2026 list (English and Arabic PDFs) enumerates all 31 protectorates with declaration year, area, governorate, management type and declaring/amending decrees; this matches the count of 31 (up to 2025) stated on the EEAA protectorates page. The list appears complete for nationally declared protectorates. It is a PDF table, not a dataset, and gives no coordinates or boundaries.

areas.designationLabel: Sustainable use of natural resources protected Area

legalStatus.text: Declared under Law No. 102 of 1983 on Natural Protectorates by Prime Minister's Decree No. 4419 of 2025

areas.notes: EEAA serial no. 31; governorate: Red Sea. EEAA: declaration of the whole Egyptian fringing coral reef ('الحيد المرجاني الحافي') as a natural protectorate. Newest protectorate (2025). Press reports (not official, not used as evidence) describe the 2025 decree as adding marine areas around protectorates declared by decrees 450/1986, 143/2003 and 1618/2006; its exact relation to Elba, Wadi El-Gemal and Northern Red Sea Islands is not verified.

gaps: No official coordinates or boundaries were found; the EEAA protectorates map (https://www.eeaa.gov.eg/Uploads/Topics/Files/20230308115635941.pdf, 2023) is image-only, so coordinates are left null.

Marine/coastal flags rely on EEAA's short descriptions; protectorates whose description does not mention marine or coastal waters (e.g. Zaranik/Bardawil, Ashtum El-Gamil, Burullus, Taba, Salloum Gulf, Al-Omayed) are left null rather than guessed.

The boundaries of the 2025 Great Fringing Reefs protectorate (Decree 4419/2025), and how it overlaps the existing Red Sea protectorates, were not verified from an official text; the decree itself was not obtained.
The EEAA page notes that protectorate pages are being updated; the English 'Regulations' PDF on the page is image-only and was not used.
Arabic local names come from a PDF whose text extraction breaks lam-alef ligatures; they were corrected by hand and should be spot-checked.
Ramsar, World Heritage and Biosphere overlaps are mentioned only where EEAA text or well-known coincidence supports them; the coordinator should confirm them from Ramsar/UNESCO.

Wikidata QIDs were checked one by one with Special:EntityData (label incl. Arabic, P17=Egypt, P31). No item was found for Nile River Islands, Gebel Kamil Meteorite or Great Fringing Reefs. The Dababiya, Salloum and Bahariya items are bare protected-area items without coordinates. Elba also has a second, bare item (Q117258352) besides the one used (Q47069184). Omayed's item is typed as a biosphere reserve but carries the protectorate's Arabic name.
